subject: [PATCH v2] mm: page_alloc: make defrag_mode retries follow the promoted order

reviews.author: Andrew Morton
reviews.summary: Reviewer Andrew Morton questioned whether the patch should be applied to stable and 7.3-rcX kernels due to its size, suggesting caution before applying such a large change.

2026-10-06.patch_summary: This patch modifies the behavior of page allocation in defrag_mode to make retries follow the promoted order, rather than the original request order. This change is intended to prevent indefinite retrying by requests that are not movable, which can lead to high memory pressure and OOM killing. The patch also updates the retry logic for direct reclaim and compaction to take into account the promoted order, and resets the retry counters when a fallback attempt is made. As a result of this change, the number of should_reclaim_retry() calls and peak memory pressure are significantly reduced, leading to improved system performance.
